items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Activate Dante Fabbro By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets activated defenseman Dante Fabbro from the injured reserve. Columbus had an open roster spot, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. Fabbro, 28, has been recovering from a broken hand suffered in preseason. The right-handed blueliner will return after missing the first four weeks of the regular season and the Blue Jackets’ first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign. Based on line rushes from practice, Fabbro will play on Columbus’ bottom pairing next to Erik Gudbranson . Fabbro will begin his ninth NHL season and second full season with the Blue Jackets. Columbus claimed Fabbro off waivers from the Nashville Predators around this time a few years ago. The early stages of his tenure with the Blue Jackets were promising. Fabbro typically played with Zach Werenski , allowing him to score nine goals and 26 points in 62 games with a +23 rating, averaging 21:39 of ice time per game. He also earned a 91.7% on-ice SV% at even strength, one of his career-best marks. Given his chemistry with Werenski, Columbus quickly signed Fabbro to a four-year, $16.5MM ($4.125MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, he didn’t play as well last season. Fabbro finished the 2025-26 campaign with five goals and 11 points in 74 games with a -16 rating, averaging 16:34 of ice time per game. He continued to block shots at a high rate, but nearly every offensive and defensive metric fell. Regardless, the Blue Jackets continue to inch toward a healthy defensive corps. After activating Fabbro, defenseman Ivan Provorov is the only defenseman left on the injured reserve as he continues to recover from a lower-body injury.

items.title: Panthers coach Paul Maurice goes to bat for Jets after Hellebuyck saga
items.summary: Paul Maurice doesn’t think Winnipeg suddenly has become a bad place to play in the aftermath of the Connor Hellebuyck saga.
items.body: Paul Maurice doesn't think Winnipeg suddenly has become a bad place to play in the aftermath of the Connor Hellebuyck saga. The Florida Panthers coach, in the Manitoba capital to take on his former team, was asked about Hellebuyck's trade demand and eventual deal last week to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday. "I know the guys that play for the Winnipeg Jets ; the guys in that room love playing here. That's been true," said Maurice, who coached the Jets from 2014 to 2021. "Take a look at a guy like (Jets captain) Adam Lowry. I think sometimes, unfortunately, we have to take notice of the players that leave, but probably like you did this weekend (at the Heritage Classic), celebrate some of the great Jets that have been here, and you've got some great ones in your room." Over the years, things haven't always ended well with prominent Jets players. However, guys like Hellebuyck, Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor did sign extensions with the small-market franchise. Maurice has maintained a deep connection to Winnipeg, saying, "If I could have one more thing, it's for the Winnipeg Jets to win the Stanley Cup," in a Sportsnet television interview on the ice after the Panthers captured their first of back-to-back titles in 2023. He was Hellebuyck's coach in Winnipeg when the goaltender broke into the league in 2015. "I don't know if it's (players) repeatedly wanting out. It's true in every market; it's just very personal for you when it happens," Maurice said. "When you're on a roll, everybody loves it. If you're not on a roll, nobody loves it. Doughty hasn’t had an agent since his eight-year, $56MM extension ahead of the 2011-12 campaign. Doughty represented himself for his current eight-year, $88MM contract, which expires at season’s end. items.title: Kindel practices with Penguins, wants to ‘move forward’ following health scare
items.summary: CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel practiced with the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday for the first time since losing consciousness while aboard the team plane one week ago.
items.body: Forward could return Thursday after losing consciousness on team plane last week CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel practiced with the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday for the first time since losing consciousness while aboard the team plane one week ago. The 19-year-old forward took full contact during a session that lasted more than an hour. He has missed two games since Oct. 20, when he experienced a vasovagal syncope, a common cause of fainting that occurs when a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure results in reduced blood blow to the brain. "Felt pretty good," Kindel said. "Was nice to be back out there with the guys and preparing for this weekend. ... I wouldn't say it's that tough. For me, it's in the past now. It's out of my head. Can't control what happened. Just have to move forward. "That's where my head's at. Just looking to move forward now. So, I'm definitely not dwelling on anything or have anything holding me back coming into this weekend." One day after playing 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Oct. 19, Kindel fell unconscious for about 10 minutes shortly after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. He received oxygen before an emergency medical landing and was transported to the University of Utah Hospital. Kindel said he began working out one or two days after collapsing. "Obviously, an interesting experience," Kindel said. "I think the Penguins kind of explained it pretty good in their releases and (general manager Kyle Dubas') press conference and everything. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Reimer made his New York Rangers debut Monday night against the Los Angeles Kings , but he was pulled after he gave up three goals on eight shots in the opening frame. The Rangers lost 6-3, and head coach Mike Sullivan pointed the blame at himself in the post-game media availability. “For (Reimer) to come in the way he has, in short order, and to go into a game like this. It’s not an easy challenge. It’s a tough challenge. I just felt the game was going, I just felt like maybe (Reimer) needs a little more preparation before we put him in that circumstance,” he said. It’s been a whirlwind two weeks for Reimer. He was signed to a professional tryout with the Hartford Wolf Pack , the Rangers’ AHL affiliate; became the oldest AHL goalie to record a shutout in nearly 20 years, then signed a one-year contract with the Rangers on Sunday. New York needed a goaltender after former Vezina Trophy winner Igor Shesterkin suffered a season-ending injury earlier this month. Including Monday’s game, Reimer has a 232-191-67 record with a .909 save percentage (SV%) and 2.88 goals against average (GAA) in 540 career games with the Rangers, Ottawa Senators , Anaheim Ducks , Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks , Carolina Hurricanes , Florida Panthers and Toronto Maple Leafs . Reimer, a native of Morweena, Man., is 5-5 with a .925 SV% and 2.70 GAA in 11 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He led the Leafs through seven games in a first-round, seven-game series against the Boston Bruins in 2013. New York is 7-6-1 with 15 points through their first 14 games of 2026-27. They have a five-day break then host the Edmonton Oilers Sunday at Madison Square Garden.

items.title: Nikishin, Hurricanes end stalemate with one-year contract
items.summary: Alexander Nikishin signed a one-year, $3 million contract with the Carolina Hurricanes on Sunday.
items.body: Defenseman was restricted free agent, helped Carolina win Stanley Cup as rookie Alexander Nikishin signed a one-year, $3 million contract with the Carolina Hurricanes on Sunday. The 25-year-old defenseman has yet to play this season. He became a restricted free agent July 1 after he had 33 points (11 goals, 22 assists) and averaged 18:11 of ice time in 81 regular-season games as a rookie last season. His 11 goals set a Carolina/Hartford Whalers record for a rookie at his position ahead of Justin Faulk 's eight in 66 games of the 2011-12 season and his 33 points were second to Brad Shaw's 35 for the Whalers in 1989-90. Nikishin was on the ice with teammates for the first time this season on Tuesday as an extra at the morning skate prior to the Hurricanes hosting the Boston Bruins (8 p.m. ET; ESPN, SN360). Carolina (9-2-2) leads the NHL with 20 points. "It's been hard, obviously, overall," Nikishin said Tuesday in comments translated by Hurricanes forward Andrei Svechnikov . "Being without the team, in America just waiting and not knowing what is going to happen. It was hard, but now it's all good." Nikishin, named to the 2025-26 NHL All-Rookie Team, had one assist in 17 Stanley Cup Playoff games to help the Hurricanes win their first championship since 2006. "He said he’s ready," Svechnikov said. "He (wants) to play sooner, but he's got to do the program, skating and practicing. Hopefully he can play soon." A third-round pick (No. 69) by Carolina in the 2020 NHL Draft, Nikishin made his NHL debut on May 15, 2025, playing 10:33 in a 3-1 win against the Washington Capitals in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Second Round that sent the Hurricanes to the Eastern Conference Final. items.title: Flyers place Rasmus Ristolainen on IR, activate Cam York
items.summary: York has been out of action for close to three weeks while recovering from an upper-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Some roster shuffling on the blue line in the City of Brotherly Love. On Tuesday, the Philadelphia Flyers announced that the team has placed defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen on injured reserve, while fellow rearguard Cam York has been activated from IR. The Flyers called up forward Jacob Gaucher from their American Hockey League affiliate, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms, as well. York has been on IR since last Sunday, which was retroactive to his last appearance in the lineup on Oct. 8. The 25-year-old has been out of action due to an upper-body injury. In the eight games he has missed, the Flyers have finally put themselves in the win column, but they continue to struggle against some of the better teams in the NHL. Philadelphia went 3-4-1 with York out of the lineup, but remain at the bottom of the Eastern Conference in win percentage. The former Michigan Wolverine failed to score a point in his first five games of the 2026-27 season. He has a plus/minus of -6 while averaging 21:49 of ice time per game, ranking third on the team. Even though he’d be eligible to return as early as this coming weekend, it was announced on Monday that Ristolainen will be out for the next two weeks with an upper-body injury of his own. The 31-year-old already missed nine games earlier this season with a hand injury before re-aggravating it last Saturday in a 5-4 loss to the Anaheim Ducks . The Finnish rearguard has yet to register a point in four appearances, averaging just over 17 minutes of ice time. York will be eligible to return to the lineup on Tuesday night, as the Flyers (3-7-3) take on the Columbus Blue Jackets in a battle between two of the worst teams in the East thus far.

items.body: Register Login Oilers’ Zach Hyman Leaves Game With Injury By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 8:30 am The Edmonton Oilers lost another forward to injury last night against the Detroit Red Wings. Partway through the second period, winger Zach Hyman exited prematurely after being hit by Red Wings defenseman Andreas Englund . Later in the evening, Jason Gregor of the Jason Gregor Show said Hyman is expected to miss at least a week with a concussion. Still, the Oilers haven’t specified Hyman’s injury or his potential recovery timeline. The hit didn’t appear very malicious ( video link ). The two players met at the blue line, and Englund pushed Hyman into the boards. Still, Hyman hit his head the wrong way on the plexiglass, immediately beginning to grab the back of his head and falling to the ice. Hyman has suffered multiple upper-body injuries throughout his career, but this would be his first documented concussion. Even if he only misses a week, it’s another troubling blow to the Oilers and Hyman. The 12-year veteran recently returned from an upper-body injury and had scored one goal in his first six games of the 2026-27 campaign. Edmonton should get some short-term relief in his absence, as Jason Dickinson is expected to return from a lower-body injury tomorrow. Still, the Oilers can’t catch their breath. On offense, once Dickinson returns, Hyman will join Mattias Janmark and Matthew Savoie in the press box. items.summary: Byfuglien returned to Winnipeg as part of the Heritage Classic festivities this past weekend.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources One of the game’s most unique specimens is feeling grateful after an exciting weekend and a return to his second home. Winnipeg, you gave us something this weekend that I didn’t realize how much I needed. A goodbye we never really got to have. The way our chapter in Winnipeg ended wasn’t how any of us imagined it would. There were a lot of emotions, a lot left unsaid, and a goodbye that never really happened. For years, I’ve carried a little sadness about that. Not because of the hockey, but because of the people. Because Winnipeg was never just about hockey to us. “It was a city that embraced our family, watched our children grow, celebrated with us, and stood behind us through so many incredible years. items.title: 10 NHL players who experienced post-hype breakouts in salary cap era
items.summary: They looked like potential busts before the lights switched on several years after they were drafted.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Oct 8, 2026; Buffalo, New York, USA; Buffalo Sabres center Tage Thompson (72) before the start of the third period against the Dallas Stars at KeyBank Center. Mandatory Credit: Timothy T. Ludwig-Imagn Images Is 2026-27 the Year of the Late Bloomer? Several prominent players who have taken longer than planned to realize their NHL potential seem to be having their moments this season. Alexis Lafreniere, the 2020 Draft’s No. 1 overall pick, has emerged as the New York Rangers’ top forward. Bruising power forward Vasiliy Podkolzin has earned a prominent role with his second NHL team, the Edmonton Oilers , and is on track to destroy his career highs in less than half a season. Sniper Jack Quinn looks like one of the Buffalo Sabres’ most important players right now. Jesper Wallstedt is poised for a Vezina Trophy push as the Minnesota Wild’s starting goaltender, two years after he was barely meeting the standard of play in the AHL, let alone the NHL. What caused these post-hype breakouts for highly touted first-round picks? Lafreniere needed an increase in coach trust . Wallstedt played much better once he had NHL defensemen protecting him rather than AHL ones. The reasons are numerous. But these four players offer hope for any fan base wondering if their top prospects are ever going to become go-to players. And they aren’t the only examples of post-hype breakouts in recent memory. items.title: Oilers thwarted by rookie Red Wings goalie as depth salvages point
items.summary: The Oilers’ young guys looked pretty good, but the one between the pipes for the Red Wings looked better.
items.body: EDMONTON — If you came away with anything from the Edmonton Oilers ’ 4-3 shootout loss to the Detroit Red Wings Monday night, it was that the young guys looked pretty good. The only problem was, the young guy who looked the best was 24-year-old Michal Postava, the goaltender making his first National Hockey League start in the Red Wings’ net. “He’s solid,” said Ryan Nugent-Hopkins , the third Oiler to be thwarted by Postava in the shootout, allowing Lucas Raymond’s wrist shot past Tristan Jarry to stand up as the game-winner. “I thought he was good positionally and always there. Even in the shootout, I saw both Connor and Leo deke, and he stuck with it. I tried to beat him with a shot and he was right there.” Postava was better than excellent, robbing Evan Bouchard twice in overtime, then stopping each of Connor McDavid , Leon Draisaitl and Nugent-Hopkins in the shootout. He’s an undrafted rookie from a Czech town of 25,000, who the Oilers had interest in when he chose Detroit. You never know with goalies — whether he goes on to greatness or becomes a one-game wonder — but if nothing else Postava will have a heck of a tale to tell the grandchildren one day. “It’s amazing, I feel like a kid,” he beamed post-game. “I watched all those NHL games when I was young and I didn’t expect to one day be in the net and win the game. items.body: Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews is pushing back on the third-period penalty called against him in Monday's loss to the Calgary Flames. Matthews was called for delay-of-game midway through the final frame with his Maple Leafs trailing by one goal — the seventh penalty assessed to Toronto and negating a power play that had only just begun for the Maple Leafs. On-ice officials determined that the 29-year-old played the puck with his glove following a faceoff, which results in a delay-of-game penalty per NHL Rule 67.2. "I think you've got to be sure 100 per cent," he said to reporters after the game in Calgary. "I fall. I don't even know what exactly the rule is, if you have to cover it or whatever, but I've got a lot of respect for the refs. They're going to make what they feel is the right call. They're not perfect, but obviously in that situation, I feel like you really gotta be sure." Matthews said he wasn't given an explanation after his penalty. The official rule states that a player shall be assessed a minor penalty if he attempts to win a face-off by batting the puck with his hands. The two players involved in the actual face-off (the centres) are not permitted to play the puck with their hand without incurring a penalty under this rule until such time as a third player (from either team) has at least touched the puck. Once the face-off is deemed complete (and a winner of the face-off is clear) hand passes shall be enforced as per Rule 79 – Hand Pass. The Carolina Hurricanes goalie is off to a 7-0-0 start and can maintain his perfect record when the defending Stanley Cup champions host the Boston Bruins at Lenovo Center on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; ESPN, SN360). "I'm happy to be playing because I only played nine games last season and that was tough mentally," Kochetkov said last week in Edmonton. "But it was actually good to see a game from the outside and it teaches you. Now when I have a bad night, I just think about how it's better to have a bad night than to not be playing at all. "I'm happy that I'm on this team and I'm happy I'm able to play. I don't think about too many other things now, I just think about hockey." items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Marchenko, Suniev, Chabot By Gabriel Foley | at October 26, 2026 9:16 pm The Toronto Maple Leafs will hold their breath after forward Kirill Marchenko exited Monday night’s game against the Calgary Flames with a lower-body injury. Marchenko sustained the injury on a hit from Flames forward Yegor Sharangovich . The hit bent his left leg awkwardly as he slid into the boards. Marchenko stretched his leg on the bench and attempted to return to the game but immediately turned around and headed towards the locker room per David Alter of The Hockey News . Losing Marchenko would deal a major blow to the Toronto offense. He was one of three Maple Leafs scoring above a point-per-game rate, entering Monday’s game with 14 points in 13 games. His absence would likely promote reigning first-overall pick Gavin McKenna back into Toronto’s top-six. McKenna has scored a productive eight points in 13 games to start his career. Finding out details of Marchenko’s injury will become the headline of Toronto’s week ahead.

This week, we feature Los Angeles Kings defenseman Drew Doughty. WASHINGTON -- As Drew Doughty approaches his 37th birthday on Dec. 8, the Los Angeles Kings defenseman naturally has reasons to contemplate how much longer he wants to continue playing. Doughty has seen longtime teammates and peers retire and this, his 19th NHL season, is the final season of his eight-year, $88 million contract ($11 million average annual value). But he believes he has a few more seasons left in him. “I think I can play until over 40,” Doughty said last week. “I believe I can. I’ve just got to stay healthy. The want to do it hasn't dropped, so, until I lose that, I'm not going to retire.” Like former teammates Dustin Brown (18 seasons) and Anze Kopitar (20 seasons), Doughty hopes to play his entire career with Los Angeles, the team that selected him with the No. 2 pick in the 2008 NHL Draft and with which he won the Stanley Cup in 2012 and 2014 and the Norris Trophy as the League’s top defenseman in 2016. items.body: Team honors forward who played 12 seasons in NHL, 8 with Rangers The New York Ranges honored the late Ron Duguay with a pregame moment of silence before Monday’s matchup against the Los Angeles Kings at Madison Square Garden. The former forward, who played 12 seasons in the NHL and eight with the Rangers, died Thursday at the age of 69 . Prior to puck drop, the team showed an array of photos of Duguay on the big screen as fans rose to their feet and gave the former forward an ovation after the moment of silence. A moment of silence in honor of one of the most beloved players in Rangers history 💙❤️ pic.twitter.com/CSccKevXMQ Duguay's family was in attendance at the game, and was honored with an ovation during a break in the action. Welcoming the family of Ron Duguay 💙❤️ pic.twitter.com/0nHYAz7JUy "The New York Rangers organization mourns the loss of Ron Duguay, one of the most popular players in franchise history," the Rangers said in a statement. "Ron's signature skating style -- with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice -- captivated The Garden Faithful, and his skill, tenacity, and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers. We join the hockey community in sending our condolences to Ron's friends, family, and loved ones during this difficult time." During his time with the Rangers, Duguay helped the team advance to the 1979 Stanley Cup Final, a five-game loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He retired from hockey in 1988-89, then served as a Rangers analyst on MSG Network for 12 years.

items.body: NEW YORK -- The National Hockey League today announced the launch of NHL Monday Night Hockey, a new initiative that will bring NHL games to hockey fans across Europe live in local prime time viewing windows on Monday nights throughout the 2026-27 season. The League and its international media partners will deliver 11 NHL Monday Night Hockey broadcasts to fans across Europe starting Monday, Nov. 30, with each game scheduled to face off in the evening across European time zones and in the afternoon in North America. The inaugural broadcast takes place on Nov. 30, at 7 p.m. CET (6 p.m. GMT in the UK and 8 p.m. EET in Finland) as Germany's Tim Stutzle and the Ottawa Senators visit Nashville to take on the Predators, featuring Switzerland’s Roman Josi and Sweden’s Filip Forsberg . A total of 11 games featuring 16 different NHL clubs will be presented over the course of the 2026-27 regular season, providing a recurring, primetime Monday-evening appointment-viewing destination for fans across Europe. NHL Monday Night Hockey complements the already established NHL Saturday and NHL Sunday presented by Fastenal European primetime games and creates a unique weekday matinee experience for fans in North America. The inaugural season will showcase many of the League's biggest stars, including Sebastian Aho , Aleksander Barkov , Leo Carlsson , Rasmus Dahlin , Victor Hedman , Martin Necas , William Nylander , David Pastrnak , JJ Peterka , Juraj Slafkovsky and Linus Ullmark . items.title: Dustin Byfuglien pens message to Jets fans after alumni-game return
items.body: The longtime Jets defenceman returned to Winnipeg ahead of Sunday's Heritage Classic for the alumni game against former Montreal Canadiens players, an experience Byfuglien called "a goodbye we never really got to have." "Winnipeg, you gave us something this weekend that I didn't realize how much I needed," Byfuglien wrote in a statement released by the Jets on Monday . "The way our chapter in Winnipeg ended wasn’t how any of us imagined it would. There were a lot of emotions, a lot left unsaid, and a goodbye that never really happened. For years, I’ve carried a little sadness about that. Not because of the hockey, but because of the people." Byfuglien played nine seasons for the Jets organization (one of which was in Atlanta prior to their relocation), during which time he earned all four of his all-star nods. He held the franchise record for most points for a defenceman until March 2026, when Josh Morrissey earned his 417th point. His time in Winnipeg came to an abrupt end ahead of the 2019-20 season, when he was granted an indefinite personal leave of absence. He then underwent season-ending surgery and, in April 2020, agreed to terminate his contract with the Jets. "I know the ending was complicated. I know there were feelings on all sides. But this weekend reminded me that sometimes the love and memories you leave behind are bigger than the way a chapter ends," Byfuglien said. "And maybe that’s what made this weekend so emotional. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Los Angeles’ Brandt Clarke interfered with Dylan Garand by pushing his glove which was covering the puck, causing it to enter the net . The decision was made in accordance of Rule 69.7, which states in part, “In the event that a goalkeeper has been pushed into the net together with the puck by an attacking player after making a stop, the goal will be disallowed.”

items.title: James Reimer pulled after first period in Rangers debut
items.body: NEW YORK — James Reimer had an abbreviated debut with the New York Rangers on Monday night, lasting just one period. The 38-year-old was pulled after giving up three goals on eight shots against Los Angeles. Dylan Garand replaced Reimer to make a ninth appearance in as many games. Making his 493rd career regular-season NHL start dating to his debut with Toronto in 2010, Reimer allowed goals to Trevor Ward and Brandt Clarke on the first two Kings shots he faced. Drew Doughty made it three, and Erik Haula clanked a shot off the post with 70 seconds left before intermission. Reimer was fast-tracked to try to provide a respite for Garand, who had started every game since franchise goalie Igor Shesterkin went down with a season-ending injury on Oct. 9 at Washington. “We’re asking a lot of Dylan,” coach Mike Sullivan said after his team's morning skate. “He just had seven starts in a row, and there’s a certain attention, focus that’s required with the goaltending position." Reimer signed a professional tryout agreement with New York's top affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack of the American Hockey League, on Oct. 15. He had a 35-save shutout for them on Saturday night. The Rangers signed Reimer on Sunday and decided to play him immediately. “We feel, just based on our discussions with our goalie coaches both in Hartford and here that Reims is in a position and he’s ready to go in the net and help us win,” Sullivan said. “He obviously has a significant body of work in the league. Defenceman Thomas Chabot shed his non-contact jersey during Monday's practice and is trending in the right direction, head coach Travis Green told reporters . Chabot was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the "C" in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. Røndbjerg, 27, has been a frequent call-up by the Golden Knights for the past few years, particularly when the team runs into injury trouble. With winger Victor Olofsson out for the foreseeable future with an upper-body injury, Vegas has had to lean on its forward depth. Still, the Golden Knights haven’t yet used Røndbjerg this season. His most recent NHL playing time came last season, when he registered one assist in four games for Vegas while averaging 12:05 of ice time per game. Throughout his career, Røndbjerg has scored three goals and 11 points in 80 games, all with the Golden Knights. The Rungsted, Denmark, native has understandably performed better with AHL Henderson. A reliable tertiary scorer, Røndbjerg has registered 65 goals and 147 points in 283 AHL contests with a +15 rating. This season, Røndbjerg has tallied two assists in seven games. Despite the call-up, Røndbjerg is unlikely to play unless the Golden Knights sustain another forward injury. Meanwhile, Holtz returns to the AHL after two games with Vegas. Filling in for Mitch Marner , who was out for the birth of his child, Holtz registered one assist in two games with a -1 rating, averaging 11:47 of ice time per game. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis NHL Central Scouting has released its annual preliminary watch list , with more than 400 names earning early recognition. However, the list arrives ahead of a busy scouting stretch, with the QMJHL Top Prospects Game scheduled for later this week before the CHL/USA Prospects Challenge gets underway in early December. The watch list breaks prospects into distinct tiers: A (projected first-rounder), B (second-to-third-rounder), C (fourth-to-fifth-rounder), and W (sixth-to-seventh-rounder). items.body: Goalie not ruled out from three-game road trip that begins Tuesday after blockbuster trade with Jets NEWARK, N.J. -- Connor Hellebuyck doesn’t feel like he needs more time before making his New Jersey Devils debut. The 33-year-old goalie practiced with the Devils for the first time on Monday after being traded from the Winnipeg Jets on Friday. "If you're asking me, I'm ready today," Hellebuyck said. "But I don't make every decision around here." Hellebuyck did not report to Jets training camp last month and spent several weeks skating in Michigan. He wore a temporary Devils sticker on his mask at practice and is thrilled to exchange informal sessions for a team environment. "It was fun," Hellebuyck said. "I've been really looking forward to this day for a while now, and it felt good getting acclimated with a new group and having some fun out there." New Jersey (7-4-0) begins a three-game road trip against the Dallas Stars on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; Prime Video, MSGSN). Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said Hellebuyck looked sharp but cautioned several decisions must be made before placing him in the lineup. The road trip continues at the Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday and concludes at the Vegas Golden Knights on Friday. "I think the intent would be to get him involved in this trip," Keefe said. items.title: Hurricanes GM Eric Tulsky talks about why Alexander Nikishin’s contract extension took so long
items.summary: Nikishin’s absence from the Hurricanes ended Sunday with a one-year, $3 million contract.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images Looming contract and trade situations have been getting resolved en masse throughout the NHL in the past couple of weeks, including one involving the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . On Sunday, defenseman Alexander Nikishin ended his holdout by signing a one-year, $3 million contract that will walk him to a version of restricted free agency where he would be eligible to sign an offer sheet and would have arbitration rights. Nikishin had neither of those options this year, limiting his leverage even as he requested a trade away from the Hurricanes. The Hurricanes reportedly attempted to use Nikishin as a trade chip to land star goalie Connor Hellebuyck, who was ultimately dealt to the New Jersey Devils last Friday. On Monday’s episode of The Sheet , hosts Jeff Marek and Greg Wyshynski were joined by Hurricanes general manager Eric Tulsky to discuss the resolution of Nikishin’s contract situation. Jeff Marek: “One of the questions that everyone’s asking: why did it take until late October? Eric Tulsky: “Sometimes it takes time to work through a process. We had a lot of different things we were looking at. We had to work through it, had to sort of get to a place that everyone was comfortable with. And that happens at a different pace in different negotiations.” Jeff Marek: “What was it? But was an agent change a factor that sort of paused things? Does that ever significantly pause things? Eric Tulsky : “You definitely have a little bit of a reset when there’s the change because the new agent needs to get up to speed on the file and talk to everybody and make sure he understands the position. And so that means you’ve got a little bit more work to do. Iit’s a little bit of a reason for the delay.

items.title: Draisaitl, Cooley, Fowler named NHL’s three stars of the week
items.body: Edmonton Oilers centre Leon Draisaitl, Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley and Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler have been named the NHL's three stars of the week. Draisaitl scored a league-best six goals and added three assists over three games as the Oilers won twice and moved into first place in the Pacific Division. The 30-year-old posted his eighth career five-point performance in a 6-5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday and enters the week riding a six-game goal streak. Cooley stopped 66 of 68 shots across two starts to post a 1.00 goals-against average and .971 save percentage while helping the Flames extend their winning streak to three games. Fowler went 2-0-0 with a 1.00 goals-against average last week. He made 33 saves in a 2-1 win over the Jets at the 2026 Heritage Classic in Winnipeg, where the 21-year-old became the youngest goaltender to start an outdoor NHL game.

Hellebuyck told reporters that he's ready to play . The goalie had been working out with former NHLers Robby Fabbri and Antonio Stranges while awaiting a trade from Winnipeg. New Jersey traded for the three-time Vezina Trophy winner from the Jets on Friday for prospect Alexander Command, goalie Nico Daws, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick. The Devils play a back-to-back against the Dallas Stars and Colorado Avalanche on Tuesday and Wednesday, then finish their road trip against the Vegas Golden Knights on Friday.

items.body: Winning is becoming a way of life for the Carolina Hurricanes . The Canes, of course, captured the Stanley Cup about four months ago, validating several seasons of high-end hockey with that elusive title. If you thought Carolina might be slowed by a championship hangover — a guilty hand is going up right here — think again. The Storm Boys walloped the St. Louis Blues 4-0 in Missouri on Saturday and sit comfortably atop a Metropolitan Division that got a bit tougher over the weekend (more on that later). Even without a game on Sunday, the Hurricanes still scored a ‘W’ by inking 25-year-old defenceman Alexander Nikishin — a restricted free agent who had not played this season — to a one-year deal worth $3 million. Considering Nikishin’s ask was thought to be somewhere in the Zeev Buium range — the young Canucks blue-liner signed an extension worth $75 over eight years in early September — it’s easy to see this one-year pact as a coup for Canes GM Eric Tulsky and his front office. Now, if you want to look at this through a different lens, it’s fair to wonder if the optimal outcome with Nikishin was to make him part of a package to acquire goalie Connor Hellebuyck from Winnipeg. Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reported during the protracted Hellebuyck saga that if Nikishin was willing to sign an extension with the Jets, the deal could well have got done. items.title: Hughes hears boos, cheers during Vancouver homecoming with Wild
items.summary:
VANCOUVER -- Quinn Hughes heard a lot of boos in his first game back in Vancouver, but a mixture of cheers during a first period tribute video is how the Minnesota Wild defenseman will remember an emotional night.
Even more than reaching the 500 points in the NHL.
items.body: Defenseman began career with Canucks before trade to Minnesota last season VANCOUVER -- Quinn Hughes heard a lot of boos in his first game back in Vancouver, but a mixture of cheers during a first period tribute video is how the Minnesota Wild defenseman will remember an emotional night. Hughes was booed steadily from the time he first stepped on the ice for warmups, when he was shown on the scoreboard during the national anthems, and every time he touched the puck in a 4-2 Minnesota win against the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday. But the booing turned to a mix of cheers and some standing ovations during the video tribute, and it did not go unnoticed. "I was just proud," said Hughes, who skated out from the Wild bench and saluted the crowd with a raised stick. "And obviously I was here for six-and-a-half years, tried my best. And got some cheers there. That was cool for me." Hughes scored on the power play at 12:55 of the second period to put the Wild ahead 3-0 for his 500th point in his 520th game, making him the seventh fastest defenseman all-time -- and second fastest American defenseman after Brian Leetch (496 games) -- to reach the milestone. He added an assist by sending Kirill Kaprizov in on a breakaway for his NHL-leading 13th goal of the season to make it 4-0 at 3:38 of the third period to make it 501 points (69 goals, 432 assists). "I wasn't thinking about it like that," he said of the milestone. "I just wanted to get a win … and then I think just seeing the fans and being able to play here again was pretty cool for me. But as far as 500 points, where that happened, it happened." Today, a look at games for the fifth week of the regular season. Highlights include the Boston Bruins visiting the Carolina Hurricanes, two of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, and Connor McDavid looking to extend his point streak with the Edmonton Oilers against the Calgary Flames on "Wednesday Night Hockey" on Prime in Canada. Boston Bruins at Carolina Hurricanes (8 p.m. ET; ESPN, SN360) It's a matchup of two of the hottest teams in the NHL. The Bruins (9-2-1) have an eight-game point streak, including seven wins. They are averaging 4.00 goals through 12 games this season while allowing just 2.17 per game. Jeremy Swayman has played the bulk and has shown no worse for the wear (7-1-1, 2.20 goals-against average, .920 save percentage). items.body: VANCOUVER — Quinn Hughes had listened to about 33 minutes of near-constant boos and jeers. He heard an energized crowd at Rogers Arena break out into various chants: Quinn, you suck; He’s not signing; Quit-ter. He watched as the jumbotron highlighted several disgruntled fans in retrofitted Hughes jerseys, letting the former captain know exactly where he stands with the Vancouver Canucks faithful after his departure last December. By the 34th minute of that, Hughes decided, presumably, that he had enough. items.body: 21-year-old helps defeat Jets, becomes youngest goalie to win outdoor game WINNIPEG -- Jacob Fowler didn’t want the night to end even though the Montreal Canadiens were clinging to a one-goal lead as time was winding down at the 2026 Tim Hortons Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium here Sunday. The Montreal Canadiens goalie soaked up as much of the atmosphere as he could in the 2-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets, becoming the youngest goalie to play and win an NHL outdoor game. “This game was different than a lot of other games I played where a lot of times, you’re looking at the clock kind of waiting for it to run out,” Fowler said. “Obviously you want to get the win, but I think tonight was one of those games where you never want the game to end. “It’s so fun to be out there. The two of us (defenseman Lane Hutson ) we’ve been talking about it. We wish we can play more of these. It’s so fun, it’s such a great environment, the ice was pretty good, so it’s just a lot of fun, I definitely took in my fair share of the moment there.” Fowler made 33 saves in the win, earning first star honors. At 21 years and 355 days, he was the youngest goalie in the history of the NHL to start an outdoor game. items.body: The 2026 Tim Hortons Heritage Classic was set to be a cold one and the Montreal Canadiens came prepared. The team showed up for the special outdoor game dressed as beer brewery workers, complete with full coveralls and hard hats. The outfits were a nod to the Molson family and team president Geoff Molson, a seventh generation descendant of John Molson, founder of Molson beer. The Molson family also still owns a significant portion of what is now called the Molson Coors Beverage Company. Une livraison spéciale est arrivée 🍺 A special delivery has arrived #GoHabsGo pic.twitter.com/WuHceaVOiT “I think it’s great," said Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis. "We’re very lucky to have Geoff Molson as an owner. He’s an excellent person. It was the players’ choice. I had nothing to do with that decision, and it wasn’t influenced by Geoff, but it shows how much we appreciate him. I like it." The Canadiens donned the outfits continuing with the tradition of NHL teams showing up wearing themed getups for special outdoor games like the Heritage Classic, Winter Classic and Stadium Series. The back of the coveralls showed off the word "Heritage" written in script.
